All three work. Open the three below. Each has your bookmarks with a small **status badge** and a button to move a bookmark between *To read* and *Finished* — and crucially, moving something to Finished **never deletes it**.

In **each**, do the same: find a **To read** bookmark, press **Mark as finished**, and notice how the two groups stay separated and how you navigate between them.

- **Option A — Tabs:** http://maker:4001/read-a.html
  You're on the **To read** tab; after marking one finished it leaves this tab — click the **Finished** tab to find it.

- **Option B — One list with a switch:** http://maker:4001/read-b.html
  A single list with an **All / To read / Finished** switch above it. Mark one finished, then flip the switch to see each group.

- **Option C — Two sections on one page:** http://maker:4001/read-c.html
  Both groups are always visible, stacked. Marking one finished moves it down into the **Finished** section and the counts update.

Two decisions to check: I made **newly saved bookmarks start as "To read"** (since you're usually saving to read later), and marking finished only **moves** a bookmark — it's never deleted, matching your "without deleting" requirement.

**After trying them, tell me which way of separating to-read from finished fits you best — and whether "new bookmarks start as To read" is right.**
